title: Ransomware data-recovery executive indicted for wire fraud after FBI sting
date_note: Krebs (20 Nov) says the indictment was returned "this week" in Rhode Island; the exact filing date is not stated. 19 Nov is the first publication (404 Media).
summary: The US Department of Justice says a federal grand jury in the District of Rhode Island returned an indictment charging Juan Ricardo Palacio Escobar, a Colombian national, with three counts of wire fraud. The indictment alleges his Florida data-recovery company said it never paid ransomware attackers, but he secretly negotiated and paid ransoms and kept the difference. DOJ says an undercover FBI operation was used. An indictment is only an allegation.
plain: US prosecutors say a ransomware recovery company claimed it never paid attackers but secretly paid ransoms and kept the difference. The FBI used an undercover operation. The charges are allegations.
exec: DOJ alleges a recovery firm hid that it paid ransoms and overcharged ransomware victims; the charges are allegations.
action: The FBI and CISA advise against paying ransoms, as the DOJ release notes, because payment does not guarantee data recovery or prevent future compromise or leaks.

validation.note: DOJ's own press release (25 Nov) read in full; it confirms the indictment, wire fraud counts and undercover FBI operation. Krebs and 404 Media earlier reported it.

review.note: Compared title, summary, Florida company, 3 wire fraud counts, undercover FBI, allegation wording, action against DOJ release; Krebs for date note
